page_title: REST Servers in Go: Part 7 - GraphQL

summary.title: REST Servers in Go: Part 7 - GraphQL
summary.one_liner: You learn why GraphQL addresses REST over- and under-fetching and how to build a GraphQL server in Go using the gqlgen library.
takeaways: REST over-fetching and under-fetching problems, and how a single GraphQL query endpoint addresses them.
How to set up a GraphQL schema with Query, Mutation, custom scalars, and separate input types, then generate server code with gqlgen.
How resolvers are implemented in gqlgen, and that field selection happens in generated code, so resolvers fetch full objects.
Trade-offs: GraphQL flexibility versus DoS risk, weaker HTTP caching, and less tooling than REST.
summary.summary: The article is Part 7 of a series on writing REST servers in Go, and it shows how the same task-management backend can be exposed via GraphQL instead. It motivates GraphQL by describing over-fetching and under-fetching in REST, then presents a schema with attachments and walks through building the server with the gqlgen package. It covers resolvers, the main function, and the built-in GraphQL playground. It closes with a comparison of GraphQL and REST covering tooling, caching, and security concerns.
